headline: Running is still on hold — the gap since the trail block is now stretching into a genuine off-stretch. Strength touched down once but hasn't built a rhythm. The base underneath remains large and intact.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is a big block of accumulated trail volume followed by a clear pause, with one lift breaking the silence and nothing since. The recent four-week running load sits far above the prior block, so the base is real and deep — this is not a fitness problem, it's a rhythm question. Strength has been light and infrequent across the last month, and the single recent session hasn't yet turned into a pattern. Steps stay high enough on both training and rest days to keep a meaningful background aerobic floor in place, which is why the pause reads as a scheduling gap rather than a shutdown. The cardio-load status flags detraining, but that's simply the mechanical consequence of no structured cardio logged — the demonstrated base doesn't vanish on that timescale. What's missing is momentum, not capacity.
sections.trends: The medium-term shape is a large, front-loaded trail block that spiked the recent four weeks well above the prior four, followed by an abrupt flattening. Year-to-date volume dwarfs the same point last year, so the annual trajectory is firmly upward and consistent with the long-term hybrid intent. The current stall is a local trough within a strongly rising curve — normal after a concentrated durability block — but it's now lasted long enough that the next few sessions determine whether this reads as a clean recovery valley or a drift. The shape still makes sense; it just needs re-entry to confirm it.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the associated heart rate are unchanged from the baseline, which is expected — nothing in the recent block was designed to move them, and the trail work sat almost entirely in easy aerobic territory. The current fitness question isn't threshold decay; that number holds. What hasn't been touched in a long stretch is any stimulus that would actually develop or even maintain the top end, so while threshold isn't eroding on this timescale, it also isn't advancing.
sections.zones: The trail block was almost purely Z1 with only trivial excursions higher — appropriate for a durability-focused stretch built on time on feet, and the per-session shapes confirm genuinely steady easy efforts rather than disguised intervals. Even the longest days barely nudged into Z3. That distribution served its purpose, but it also means the intensity profile has been one-dimensional for a while. The speed and threshold end of the spectrum is now conspicuously absent, and a healthy hybrid distribution needs that side to reappear before the aggregate skews permanently soft.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR remains modest and mostly low-zone, consistent with functional-fitness circuits rather than heavy grind work, though the most recent lift logged no HR at all. Where both sources exist on runs they track sensibly, and the easy trail efforts show clean, believable low-HR lines. Nothing in the sensor-source agreement is worth acting on — the readings across sources hang together fine.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the real story: a dense, clustered burst of back-to-back trail days, then a hard stop, then a single isolated lift. That's a spike-then-silence signature rather than a steady weekly cadence. For an athlete who otherwise maintains year-round readiness, the notable feature isn't the volume — it's that frequency collapsed to near zero right after the peak. Rebuilding a repeatable weekly rhythm now matters more than any single big session.
sections.personal_bests: None are within reach in the current state — every running PB lives at paces the recent block never approached, and the fast bests date from a period of dedicated speed work that hasn't been present lately. The durability PBs are more aligned with recent focus, but nothing today suggests an imminent assault on any mark. This is a base-consolidation window, not a peaking one.

watch_items: Watch whether running actually re-enters this week, or whether the gap extends further into an unplanned lay-off.
Watch whether strength converts the single recent lift into a repeated cadence rather than another isolated touch.
Watch for the first reappearance of any faster or upper-zone stimulus — the top end has now been dorment for an unusually long stretch.
Watch whether the first easy run comes back at a normal easy HR, confirming the trail block absorbed cleanly.
